❯ 3 — accounts and content from many users (eventually multi-tenant).                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  Specifics:                                                                                                                                                                                              
  - Provider: Supabase Postgres (single project), multi-schema. Four schemas locked from migration 0001:                                                                                                  
      * public    — read-only mirror of Topishop v2's data, NEVER written by PipeLogic                                                                                                                    
      * pipelogic — PipeLogic-owned config + audit (table_metadata, rules, joins, inbox_items, recipe_*, edit_history, reference_audit, etc.)                                                             
      * pl_draft  — raw imports (one table per source per bundle)                                                                                                                                         
      * pl_live   — future: computed / enriched tables (Layer 3 surface)                                                                                                                                  
  - Driver: postgres.js v3.x (tagged template literals). LOCKED — NO Drizzle, NO Prisma, NO Kysely. ADR rationale: ORMs hide the jsonb interpolation pattern that caused silent corruption in V1.         
  - Migrations: raw .sql files, applied manually via Supabase Studio. NOT auto-applied. NOT Drizzle Kit. NOT Prisma migrate.                                                                              
  - jsonb writes: custom jsonParam(x) helper, never ${JSON.stringify(x)}::jsonb (V1 had to backfill 28 corrupted rows; jsonb_typeof is the audit method).                                                 
  - Credentials at rest: AES-256-GCM from day 1, mandatory. No plaintext fallback. No "backfill later" mode.                                                                                              
  - Region: EU (data residency).                                                                                                                                                                          
  - File uploads / blob storage: NONE in v1. CSV imports are PARSED into pl_draft tables — the CSVs themselves aren't stored as files.                                                                    

⏺ That's a lot of locked-in detail — exactly the kind of thing that prevents the agent from drifting next session. I want to record it across two sections of stack.md (the data-store specifics + the
  hard rules in Architecture facts), because some of these are "X NOT Y" invariants that must survive every future turn.

  ---                                                                                                                                                                                                     
  Proposed record — .sdd/stack.md:
                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  ## Data store                       
                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  ## Data store                                                                                                                                                                                           
  
  - **Type:** Postgres                                                                                                                                                                                    
  - **Provider:** Supabase Postgres (single project, EU region for data residency)
  - **Schema layout:** four schemas, locked from migration `0001`:
    - `public` — read-only mirror of Topishop v2's data; **PipeLogic NEVER writes here**                                                                                                                  
    - `pipelogic` — PipeLogic-owned config + audit (`table_metadata`, `rules`, `joins`, `inbox_items`, `recipe_*`, `edit_history`, `reference_audit`, …)
    - `pl_draft` — raw CSV imports (one table per source per bundle)                                                                                                                                      
    - `pl_live` — future Layer 3 surface (computed / enriched tables)                                                                                                                                     
  - **Schema source:** `.sdd/data-model.md` (single source of truth for entities + fields). DDL ships as raw `.sql` files, applied manually via Supabase Studio — NOT auto-applied, NOT through Drizzle   
  Kit / Prisma migrate.                                                                                                                                                                                   
  - **Driver:** `postgres.js` v3.x (tagged-template literals). **No ORM.** See Architecture facts for the locked rationale.
  - **File / blob storage:** none in v1. CSV imports are PARSED into `pl_draft` tables; the CSV files themselves are not stored.                                                                          
  - **Why:** Postgres for relational + multi-tenant scaffolding; Supabase keeps cost flat for the MVP and unblocks RLS later; the four-schema split enforces the read-only-mirror invariant at the        
  database layer rather than relying on app-code discipline.                                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  ## Architecture facts (the AI must remember)                                                                                                                                                            
                                      
  - The `public` schema is a **read-only mirror of Topishop v2** — PipeLogic NEVER writes to `public`. If the agent ever wonders "should I write here?" the answer is no.                                 
  - DB driver is **`postgres.js` v3.x with tagged-template literals** (NOT Drizzle, NOT Prisma, NOT Kysely). Reason: ORMs hide the jsonb interpolation pattern that caused silent corruption in V1.       
  - jsonb writes go through the **`jsonParam(x)` helper** — NEVER `${JSON.stringify(x)}::jsonb`. V1 had to backfill 28 corrupted rows over this. `jsonb_typeof` is the audit method.                      
  - Migrations are **raw `.sql` files applied manually via Supabase Studio** — NOT auto-applied at deploy time, NOT Drizzle Kit, NOT Prisma migrate.                                                      
  - Credentials at rest are **AES-256-GCM, mandatory from day 1**. No plaintext fallback. No "backfill later" mode.                                                                                       
  - Database region is **EU** (data residency requirement).

  2. tenant_id from question 1 — the multi-tenant scaffolding rule says every table carries tenant_id and UNIQUE indexes always include it. Does this rule apply to all four schemas, or only pipelogic +
  pl_draft + pl_live (since public is a mirror you don't control)? I'd guess "only the three PipeLogic-owned schemas" but I want it explicit.

     ## Schema: pipelogic

                      JOINs across pipelogic.* → public.* enforce tenant_id on the pipelogic side                                                                                                         
                      (per A.6: "tenant_id in the ON clause, not just WHERE").                                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                                                                          
     When multi-tenant lands post-MVP, mapping "public's data" to a specific tenant becomes                                                                                                               
     a Layer 4 concern (likely: implicit tenant-0 mapping at the join boundary). Not v1.

         -migrations.

         +types in migrations.

  Q6.2 — Will the app send emails?

  ▎ Examples: confirmation emails, magic-link sign-in emails, password resets, weekly digests, transactional notifications, invite emails.

  yes / no / not sure

  A note before you answer: Supabase Auth itself sends magic-link / password-reset emails out of the box — but only via Supabase's built-in email provider, which is fine for early dev but capped at 4
  emails/hour and not deliverability-tuned for production. Most Supabase projects swap in a dedicated provider via SMTP config once they ship.

  So the real question is: does the app send any emails BEYOND the auth flow? (Invite emails to bring more users into the allowlist, weekly digests, error notifications, customer-comms, etc.)

  If yes — or if you want production-grade auth emails immediately — pick a provider:
  - Resend — cheapest + easiest, React Email templates work natively, ~$0/mo for low volume.
  - Postmark — best deliverability (highest inbox-placement rate), slightly pricier.
  - SendGrid — older, bigger; corporate-friendly.
  - AWS SES — cheapest at scale, more setup.
  - Just use Supabase's built-in for now, decide later — recorded as tbd, re-asked at first feature that needs email.

  Reply: yes <provider> / no / tbd / not sure.

  - You have 5 cron routes running on a schedule. If any of them silently fails (e.g. recipe-import errors after a BaseLinker token revocation), you need to know — Topishop won't see it directly, but
  their data goes stale.

  On to the final question.

  ---
  Question 7 of 7 — Want the agent to read your project state efficiently?

  The framework keeps notes in .sdd/INDEX.md, decisions.md, patterns.md, data-model.md, stack.md, etc. The agent reads them at every session start. After 3-6 months those files can grow large —
  sometimes 100k+ tokens.

  The SDD MCP server is a small Python extension that lets the agent fetch one note at a time (e.g. "the active step in feature 003", ~200 bytes) instead of re-reading whole files. Saves 40-60% on
  tokens once the project has been running a few months.

  1. Yes — turn it on (recommended) — the wizard runs bash extensions/sdd-mcp-server/enable.sh, registers the server with Claude Code (creates .mcp.json or updates ~/.claude.json), records
  parameters.mcp.enabled: true. No external service, no extra subscription.
  2. No — I'll read whole files — for very small / short-lived projects, fine.
  3. Tell me more — I explain the trade in plain English first.

  Given how much architectural context you've already loaded into stack.md / principles.md / data-model.md (this is a dense project from day 1, not a small one), Option 1 is a strong fit. The token
  savings start showing within weeks because the load surface is already substantial. HOWEVER — same caveat as Playwright in Q4: the extensions/sdd-mcp-server/ directory referenced by the brick isn't
  shipped in this template. Enabling it would require either:
  - (a) the actual extension code shipping later (and you'd run enable.sh then), or
  - (b) skipping the extension and keeping notes-as-files, but recording mcp.enabled: false for now.

  So in practice your two real choices are:
  - Yes-but-deferred — record mcp.enabled: true, intent locked, extension wires up when shipped.
  - No (record false) — read whole files; revisit later via /sdd-config.

  If you say yes, I'll skip the Tier-3 LLM-driven-synthesis sub-questions (Q1-Q4) since they require the MCP server to actually be installed, and they're an opt-in v1.1 feature anyway.

  Reply: 1 / 2 / 3, or describe in your own words.

      157 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      158 +#### §6 Non-goals (lines we hold)                                                                                                                                                       
      159 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      160 +PipeLogic explicitly **does NOT**:                                                                                                                                                      
      161 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      162 +1. **Build a visualisation layer.** Charts, dashboards, executive views — users export to Metabase / Looker / their BI tool. We are the data substrate, not the chart maker.            
      163 +2. **Provide a SQL escape hatch to end users.** If a non-technical operator needs SQL to do their job, the product has failed. Rules / joins / computed columns are always built visuall
          +y.                                                                                                                                                                                      
      164 +3. **Replace Topishop v2 in flight.** v2 stays running, untouched, throughout MVP. PipeLogic V2 reads from v2's `public.*` schema (read-only) but never writes to it. Migration path is 
          +"rewire one v2 view at a time, post-MVP, with before/after validation."                                                                                                                 
      165 +4. **Hardcode Topishop-specifics in core.** No `if channel == 'Amazon'`, no `if status == 18672` in TypeScript. Every Topishop-specific value lives in reference tables / rules / recipe
          + rows the user can rewrite. (Otherwise customer #2 costs as much as customer #1.)                                                                                                       
      166 +5. **Let AI commit on behalf of the user.** Every AI suggestion (auto-classified rows, drafted recipes, suggested joins) lands as a draft proposal. The user reviews, accepts, or reject
          +s. AI never writes to a published surface.                                                                                                                                              
      167 +6. **Real-time push (webhooks) for v1.** Cron-based refresh is sufficient for hourly / daily cadences. Webhook ingest comes later (Layer 4).                                            
      168 +7. **Tenant self-serve signup.** GetUnlocked onboards tenants via handshake (Sam talks to them, sets up the account). Self-serve is a SaaS-launch concern, not MVP.                     
      169 +8. **Mobile app.** Desktop web first. Responsive web "nice to have" but not a v1 success criterion.                                                                                     
      170 +9. **Cross-tenant analytics for customers.** Tenants see only their own data. Cross-tenant views are reserved for the GetUnlocked support team operator role.                           
      171 +10. **Excel-formula UX in v1.** Structured rule builder only. Formulas come in v2 once the structured builder proves the rules engine plumbing works.                                   
      172 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      173 +**Scope-guard propagation:** every child feature's spec.md must reference these 10 non-goals at SPEC §10 (Out-of-scope). The proxy gate is: a feature that proposes any of #1-10 is in v
          +iolation and must be re-scoped or escalated to a milestone-level decision.                                                                                                              
      174 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      175 +#### §7 Hard constraints                                                                                                                                                                
      176 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      177 +##### Operational                                                                                                                                                                       
      178 +- **Topishop v2 stays running, unchanged, throughout MVP.** Every PipeLogic change must be reversible without touching v2 behaviour. v2's `public.*` schema is **read-only** from PipeLo
          +gic's perspective.                                                                                                                                                                      
      179 +- **Topishop deadline pressure.** Each milestone has a real business cost if missed (Topishop margin reporting needs this). Plan small, ship continuously, prefer "shipped narrow" over 
          +"broad and stuck."                                                                                                                                                                      
      180 +- **Sam is the primary user AND the primary reviewer.** PRs need preview-deploy-clickable QA. Diff review doesn't work — Sam can't read code.                                           
      181 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      182 +##### Data + audit                                                                                                                                                                      
      183 +- **All credentials encrypted at rest** (AES-256-GCM) **from day 1**. No plaintext fallback. No "we'll backfill later" flag — encryption is mandatory or the credential isn't stored.   
      184 +- **Append-only audit on every mutation** to operator-controlled tables. `pipelogic.edit_history`, `pipelogic.reference_audit`, `pipelogic.import_run`, `pipelogic.recipe_provenance` — 
          +every write goes through these. **Never `DELETE` from audit tables.**                                                                                                                   
      185 +- **Recipe versions are immutable.** Once published, never modified. Changes ship as new versions. Enforced by DB trigger (UPDATE on payload columns blocked).                          
      186 +- **`tenant_id` on every table from migration 0001** with NOT NULL. **Every UNIQUE INDEX includes `tenant_id` first.** Even in single-tenant MVP — the leak risk on retrofit is real (V1
          + had to fix this).                                                                                                                                                                      
      187 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      188 +##### Compliance / privacy                                                                                                                                                              
      189 +- **No GDPR / SOC2 work in scope** for v1 MVP. (Add when first paying tenant comes onboard with compliance asks.)                                                                       
      190 +- **Customer data stays in EU region** (Supabase project region: EU). No cross-region replication.                                                                                      
      191 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      192 +##### Code quality                                                                                                                                                                      
      193 +- **Pre-commit gate:** `tsc --noEmit` + `vitest run` + (conditional) `pnpm build` + (conditional) live-DB SQL verify.                                                                   
      194 +- **Pre-push gate:** Playwright smoke on critical flows.                                                                                                                                
      195 +- **Branch protection on `main`** — every change goes through a PR. No direct pushes. Required check: "Typecheck + Test + Build."                                                       
      196 +- **PR target: ~300 lines, one logical change.** Bigger = split unless mechanical.                                                                                                      
      197 +- **No `--no-verify`** on commits unless the user explicitly asks.                                                                                                                      
      198 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      199 +##### UX                                                                                                                                                                                
      200 +- **Plain-English everywhere** in user-facing copy. No jargon, no error codes, no SHAs.                                                                                                 
      201 +- **Non-technical operator can complete every flow without reading docs** beyond a 1-line tooltip.

       76  **How to apply:** every commit must pass `tsc --noEmit` + `vitest run` (plus `pnpm build` when build-affecting files staged, plus a live-DB SQL verify when migration files staged). Eve
           ry push must pass the Playwright smoke on critical flows. **`--no-verify` is forbidden** unless the user explicitly authorises it for a single push, and the bypass is logged to `decisi
           ons.md` per A.18.                               
       77  **Adopted:** 2026-05-05                         
       78                                    
       79 -## No AI / LLM in product runtime; AI proposals are drafts only (rule A.14 P3, brief §4)                                                                                                
       79 +---                                                                                                                                                                                            
       80                                                                                                                                                                                                 
       81 +# Product principles — A.14 P1 through P8 (carry-over from V1)                                                                                                                                 
       82 +                                                                                                                                                                                               
       83 +The following 8 principles are the product's design DNA — every feature, every UX choice, every data-shape decision must obey these. If a V2 design choice violates any of them, the cho       
          +ice is wrong. (Source: V1 MVP brief, locked decision A.14.)                                                                                                                                    
       84 +                                                                                                                                                                                               
       85 +## P1 — Tables have types; each type has different UX                                                                                                                                   
       86 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
       87 +**Why:** users approach a "raw imported orders table" differently than a "carrier routing reference table" or a "computed margin view". Treating them all identically destroys the affor
          +dances each kind needs. V1 had to retrofit per-kind UX after shipping a one-size-fits-all grid.                                                                                         
       88 +**How to apply:** every table carries a `kind` (`raw` / `reference` / `view` / `mv` / `computed`). The UI surfaces:                                                                     
       89 +- `raw` — read-only grid with cell-edit only on `editable_columns` whitelist (F02)                                                                                                      
       90 +- `reference` — full editable grid at `/reference/<name>` with append-only audit (F10)                                                                                                  
       91 +- `computed` — rule-defined; not directly editable; goes through `/rules` to change behaviour (F11, F12)                                                                                
       92 +- `view` / `mv` — read-only; built from joins (F13) or materialised views (post-MVP)                                                                                                    
       93 +The `kind` lives in `pipelogic.table_metadata`. F01's swim-lane clustering on `/map` is the visual expression of P1.                                                                    
       94 +**Adopted:** 2026-05-05                                                                                                                                                                 
       95 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
       96 +## P2 — Columns are opt-in per user                                                                                                                                                     
       97 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
       98 +**Why:** non-technical operators get overwhelmed by 47-column tables imported from BaseLinker. Hiding clutter is more important than completeness. Storing every column means future fea
          +tures can use them; surfacing every column means today's user runs away.                                                                                                                
       99 +**How to apply:** every column is **stored** (the import never drops data), but the default view **hides** every column the user hasn't explicitly opted into. UI shows N visible column
          +s + a "show hidden columns" affordance. Per-user column visibility (post-multi-tenant: per-tenant + per-user). V1 lesson: never auto-decide visibility from a "looks important" heuristi
          +c — always opt-in.                                                                                                                                                                      
      100 +**Adopted:** 2026-05-05                                                                                                                                                                 
      101 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      102 +## P3 — AI drafts, user decides (rule A.14 P3, brief §4)                                                                                                                                
      103 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      104  **Why:** runtime LLM calls add latency, failure surface, vendor cost, and a non-deterministic UX layer the user can't reason about. Single-customer MVP doesn't justify any of these. Th
           e only defensible LLM uses are dev-side and review-gated.
      105  **How to apply:** product code paths NEVER call an LLM at user-action time (no auto-classify on click, no AI-suggested joins inline, no chat assistant in the UI). LLM usage is confined
            to dev-side authoring (e.g. Tier 3 / Tier 4 recipe authoring, offline). Anything an LLM produces lands as a DRAFT row that the user reviews, accepts, or rejects — never auto-applied.
           Re-evaluation requires either SDD v1.1 Tier 3 synthesis opting-in or a feature with a clear runtime-LLM ROI (none on the current 15-feature roadmap).
      106  **Adopted:** 2026-05-05
      107 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      108 +## P4 — Authority hierarchy per concept                                                                                                                                                 
      109 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      110 +**Why:** for any business question (`is_cancelled`?, `commission`?), data lives in multiple places (BaseLinker, marketplace API, courier invoice, ops-team's spreadsheet). Without a dec
          +lared hierarchy, disagreements between sources lead to silent inconsistency. The user must know which source wins — and surface disagreements when they happen.                         
      111 +**How to apply:** every concept (`is_cancelled`, `order_health`, `commission_rate`, etc.) has a declared authority hierarchy in `pipelogic.authority_hierarchy`: an ordered list of `(co
          +ncept, source, rank)` rows. When two sources disagree, the higher-rank source wins AND the disagreement gets surfaced as an inbox item (F14, health check H2 — authority-source disagree
          +ment). User can override per-row (writes to `pipelogic.edit_history`).                                                                                                                  
      112 +**Adopted:** 2026-05-05                                                                                                                                                                 
      113 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      114 +## P5 — Rules are metadata, editable like Excel                                                                                                                                         
      115 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      116 +**Why:** classification logic ("which orders are 'cancelled' vs 'pending review'?") changes constantly as the business evolves. Hardcoding it in TypeScript means every change needs a d
          +eveloper + a deploy. Storing it as data means the operator changes it themselves, in the UI, with a live preview of which rows the change affects.                                      
      117 +**How to apply:** rules live in `pipelogic.rules` as JSONB condition trees with: `name`, `condition_tree` (JSONB), `then_set` clause, `concept`, `position` (drag-reorder; first match w
          +ins), `tenant_id`. UI at `/rules` (F11) is a structured tree builder — no formula text input in v1 (per non-goal #10). Live preview shows hit count + 5 sample matches per rule.        
      118 +**Adopted:** 2026-05-05                                                                                                                                                                 
      119 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      120 +## P6 — Manual edit is first class                                                                                                                                                      
      121 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      122 +**Why:** rules cover patterns; manual edits cover the long tail of one-offs. A product that only supports rules forces users into "create a one-row rule for this single order" anti-pat
          +terns. Both modes ship together with full audit on each.                                                                                                                                
      123 +**How to apply:** every cell on every editable table can be manually edited via F02's side-panel UX, AND every edit lands in `pipelogic.edit_history` (append-only). Rules-driven values
          + and manual overrides coexist on the same cell — manual edit wins, but the rule's prediction stays visible (so the user can see "rule said X, I changed to Y"). Both rule-evaluations an
          +d manual edits are equally first-class signals — neither is the "real" answer.                                                                                                          
      124 +**Adopted:** 2026-05-05                                                                                                                                                                 
      125 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      126 +## P7 — Cross-reference visibility is the moat (the inbox)                                                                                                                              
      127 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      128 +**Why:** every operator-facing data product eventually fails the same way: a row gets imported, looks fine, never matches anything downstream, and the operator finds out three months l
          +ater when an invoice doesn't reconcile. The moat is making "didn't match" loud — surfacing every unmatched row in one place the operator visits Monday morning.                         
      129 +**How to apply:** the inbox at `/inbox` (F14) surfaces 7 health checks (H1-H7) — unmatched joins, authority-source disagreements, reference-table coverage gaps, classification-rule mis
          +ses, schema-drift events, stale-imports, etc. — each producing rows in `pipelogic.inbox_items`. UI: filterable list + bulk actions ("mark as expected", "open the source row to fix"). *
          +*This is the product's primary moat** — every other feature feeds the inbox.                                                                                                            
      130 +**Adopted:** 2026-05-05                                                                                                                                                                 
      131 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      132 +## P8 — Flexibility over hardcoded correctness                                                                                                                                          
      133 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      134 +**Why:** if customer #1 needs feature X and we hardcode `if customer == 'topishop' do_X`, customer #2 costs as much to onboard as customer #1. The platform's value is being usable by n
          +on-technical operators across different stacks. Hardcoded correctness ships fast but caps the customer count at 1.                                                                      
      135 +**How to apply:** **NO Topishop-specific constants in core code.** No `if channel == 'Amazon'`, no `if status == 18672`, no hardcoded Topishop UUIDs. Every Topishop-specific value live
          +s in reference tables / rules / recipe rows the user can rewrite. Adding a new customer = new tenant + new reference rows + new recipe bindings = zero core code changes. (Per non-goal 
          +#4.)                                                                                                                                                                                    
      136 +**Adopted:** 2026-05-05                                                                                                                                                                 
      137 +

      141 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      142 +The following are workflow and discipline rules — how the agent works, what gates fire when, who's accountable — distinct from the product-design principles above.

          the tagged-template-literal interpolation pattern that postgres.js uses for jsonb. Multiple silent-corruption bugs in V1 traced to mishandled interpolation an ORM would have hidden furt

      41  **A.2 — `jsonParam(x)` for jsonb writes, never `${JSON.stringify(x)}::jsonb`** — carried over from V1. Use the `jsonParam(x)` helper from `@/lib/db/pg.ts`. Why: `${JSON.stringify(x)}::j
          sonb` binds the pre-stringified value as a jsonb **string scalar** (not a jsonb **object**). At read time, `col->>'foo'` returns NULL silently. V1 had to backfill 28 corrupted rows in `
          recipe_provenance.details` via migration 0033. Audit method: `SELECT id, jsonb_typeof(col) FROM <table>` — `'string'` means corrupted. Already principle in `principles.md`.

  - A. Live on every panel-open: SELECT … LIMIT 50 runs at click-time. Always fresh; slowest UX (one round-trip per click).

  - C. TTL'd cache (e.g. 30s): refreshes if the panel re-opens after the TTL. Compromise.

⏺ §4 ux-brief is AGENT-LED. Drafting from §1–§3 + the locked UX direction.                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  ---                                                                                                                                                                                                     
  §4 UX & Design brief — F01 Auth + canvas shell (DRAFT for approval)                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  Built on top of §3's locked UX direction (anchors n8n + Figma + Coda; non-technical-but-app-savvy audience; M-tags win every cutting-edge conflict). My job here: translate that direction into concrete
   §4 decisions, surface 3 still-open gaps with options, recommend.                                                                                                                                       
                                             
  Tone / feel                                                                                                                                                                                             
                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  Structured, calm, content-forward. A daily-driver tool, not playful (this isn't Duolingo); not corporate-bank either (Sam isn't a banker). /map should feel like an atlas Sam can navigate — every card
  a confident, restrained component; generous whitespace; clear type hierarchy. Room-temperature of n8n's editor + breathing room of Coda's docs.                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  Reference anchors (3 + 2 anti-references)                   
                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  ┌────────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │                App                 │                                   What to borrow                                   │                               Why it maps                               │   
  ├────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ n8n (editor canvas)                │ Node-as-card visual treatment; group → cluster pattern; subtle background grid;    │ Forwards-rhymes with F13 joins UI (which IS a node-graph) — F01 should  │   
  │                                    │ pannable feel                                                                      │ set vocabulary F13 inherits                                             │
  ├────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤   
  │ Figma (file-thumbnail page /       │ Calm canvas background; soft card shadows + 8px radius; click-to-focus side panel; │ Canvas-first idiom; "card on a workspace" is a learned expectation      │   
  │ FigJam canvas)                     │  cmd+zoom; cmd+1/2 density swap                                                    │                                                                         │
  ├────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤   
  │ Coda (doc home + table-of-contents │ Block-based density; subtle dividers; warm-but-restrained color; info hierarchy    │ Content-forward typography; "everyone reads this without instruction"   │
  │  views)                            │                                                                                    │ shape                                                                   │
  └────────────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                                              
  Anti-references:                                                                                                                                                                                        
  - Linear / Superhuman — too dense; 13px type loses the app-savvy-non-technical audience (per Q5).
  - Notion (doc surface) — too document-shaped; F01 is workspace-shaped, not doc-shaped.                                                                                                                  
                                             
  Primary screen + device posture                                                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  Desktop-first. Brief non-goal #8 locks this. Primary target: MacBook Air at 1440×900. Mobile ("nice to have" per non-goal #8) gets a degraded read-only mode at SHIP, not a full mobile UX commitment in
   F01.                                                                                                                                                                                                   
                                                             
  Information density                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  Breathable. Not Vercel-dashboard-dense; not Linear-compact. Each card carries visual weight; cards have ~24–32px gutters; swim-lane (or cluster) headers have clear visual separation from contents. Per
   Q5: app-savvy-readability wins over Linear/Superhuman extremes.                                                                                                                                        
                                      
  Motion                                                                                                                                                                                                  
                                                             
  Subtle, <100ms, non-blocking {best-effort: Sam at SHIP — preview-deploy review}. Hover transitions on cards; smooth fade for the side-panel open/close; NO scroll-driven hijacks; respect               
  prefers-reduced-motion (collapse to instant). M1 wins → no blocking animation.
                                   
  Accessibility floor                                                                                                                                                                                     
                                                             
  WCAG 2.1 AA minimum.                                                                                                                                                                                    
  - Reduced-motion respect (above)    
  - Keyboard nav for every interactive element (tab + arrow + enter for cards)
  - 4.5:1 contrast for body, 3:1 for large/UI text                                                                                                                                                        
  - Focus rings visible (2px ring offset)         
  - Screen-reader-friendly card semantics (button or a, never div + onClick)                                                                                                                              
                                                                            
  No RTL / locale work in scope. Single-customer EU MVP; Topishop reads English/French; locale work lands when GetUnlocked SaaS opens.
                                             
  ---                                                        
  Three open decisions (§4 gaps that didn't close at §3)                                                                                                                                                  
                                                             
  A. Swim-lane metaphor vs alternatives (per Q3 grill — open)                                                                                                                                             
                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  You explicitly left this open at §3. Three concrete shapes:
                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  A1. Brief-faithful swim lanes. Four horizontal lanes (raw / reference / view / mv) stacked vertically. Cards pack left-to-right within each lane. Sticky lane headers while scrolling.                  
  - Pros: matches brief verbatim; familiar from Trello / Jira board.                                                                                                                                      
  - Cons: horizontal scroll within a lane at scale; visually "Trello-shaped" not "n8n-shaped" — weakens the F13 forwards-rhyme.                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  A2. Canvas-with-clusters (n8n / Figma flavour). Pannable canvas; cards grouped into 4 visually-distinct clusters (color-tinted background + soft border per cluster); zoomable; minimap in corner.
  - Pros: aesthetic match with locked anchors; forwards-rhymes with F13 joins UI; scales to 100+ tables better than swim lanes.                                                                           
  - Cons: zoom UX adds learnability cost (mitigated by minimap + first-visit onboarding tooltip); further from brief's literal "swim lanes" wording.                                                      
                                                                                                                                                    
  A3. Vertical category stacks (Coda / Vercel flavour). Single-column scroll; H2-style heading per category; cards as a 3-up grid under each heading.                                                     
  - Pros: simplest; lowest learnability; mobile fallback nearly free; reads like a doc.
  - Cons: loses workspace/canvas feel; doesn't rhyme with F13 joins.                                                                                                                                      
                                                                    
  My recommendation: A2. Best anchor match (n8n + Figma); scales to M7 wayfinding-at-N>30 cleanly; forwards-rhymes with F13. Pays a learnability tax mitigable with minimap + first-visit tooltip.        
                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  B. Theme posture — light / dark / both?                                                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  B1. Light only at F01. Smallest scope; defer dark mode to later feature.                                                                                                                                
  B2. Both light + dark from F01 (system-preference auto-switch). Aesthetic anchors all do dark well; Sam likely uses dark; Tailwind v4 + shadcn/ui make this nearly free.                                
  B3. Dark only at F01. Counter-intuitive default for non-technical users.                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  My recommendation: B2. App-savvy audience expects it; ~1 extra BUILD task to wire toggle + verify both contrasts.                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  C. Typography system                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  C1. Tailwind v4 defaults + system font. Smallest scope; legible; default-looking.                                                                                                                       
  C2. Inter (free via @fontsource/inter). Standard product-app font; rhymes with Linear / Notion / Vercel-marketing.
  C3. Geist (Vercel's font; free via @fontsource/geist). Rhymes with Vercel/Stripe anchor; geometric flavour; visually distinguishes from "yet another Inter SaaS."                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  My recommendation: C3. Strongest match with the calm/structured tone; free; visual identity matters even at MVP.                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  ---                                                                                                                                                                                                     
  End the turn with: Reply looks good (or approve A2 + B2 + C3) to lock these. Or tell me what to change — e.g. A1 instead, B1 light only, C2 Inter, tone too quiet, add color spec, swap an 
  anti-reference. Then run /next.

  Raw tally: A1 = 4✅, A2 = 5✅, A3 = 5✅. Roughly tied — but the lenses aren't equally weighted.                                                                                                         
                                      
  ---                                                                                                                                                                                                     
  What dominates the decision         
                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  Two lenses carry disproportionate weight:
                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  Lens 1 + 2 (F03 + F13 forward-compat) is the load-bearing argument. F13 is the product's MOAT — per principle P7 ("cross-reference visibility is the moat") and per the brief's own framing of F14 inbox
   as "the moat (V1 P7)." But the inbox is FED by joins. F13 IS the visual-join surface. If F01's metaphor doesn't rhyme with F13, the product breaks at the most important moment — when you go from "I  
  see my tables" to "I connect them." Sam clicks /joins and gets a completely different mental model. Bad.                                                                                                
                                      
  A2 makes F01 → F03 → F13 read as one continuous surface. A1 and A3 force F03 and F13 into being foreign islands.                                                                                        
  
  Lens 6 + 4 (build cost + learnability) is the counter-argument. A2 IS more expensive to build correctly, and the pan/zoom UX is the biggest learnability tax — exactly the "M-tags win conflicts" risk  
  in Q5.                              
                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  ---                                 
  A2-prime — the hybrid I think actually wins
                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  The drawbacks of A2 (build cost + learnability) come from one specific decision: shipping pan/zoom in F01. But pan/zoom isn't needed in F01 — it's needed in F13 (when there are edges between cards and
   you want to focus on a region). F01 only needs the visual language of a canvas, not the interactive primitives of one.                                                                                 
                                      
  A2-prime: canvas-shaped layout, no pan/zoom yet.                                                                                                                                                        
                                      
  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐                                       
  │                                   What ships in F01                                    │                           What lands later                           │
  ├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤                                       
  │ ✅ Canvas-shaped page with 4 visually-distinct tinted clusters                         │ F13 adds React Flow + pan/zoom + edge-drawing on the same surface    │
  ├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ ✅ Minimap as a static "you-are-here" overview indicator                               │ F13 makes the minimap interactive (click to jump)                    │                                       
  ├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤                                       
  │ ✅ Cards arranged on a dotted-grid background (the visual language)                    │ F13 turns cards into React Flow nodes with edges                     │                                       
  ├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤                                       
  │ ✅ Vertical scroll only (no horizontal pan, no zoom) — page acts like a doc internally │ F13 makes the canvas pannable with cmd+drag, zoomable with cmd+wheel │
  ├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤                                       
  │ ✅ Plain CSS/Tailwind — no React Flow library yet                                      │ F13 adds @xyflow/react                                               │
  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘                                       
                                      
  This A2-prime reads "2027" on first click (lens 12 ✅), rhymes with F13 vocabulary 1:1 (lens 1+2 ✅), keeps build cost in line with A3 (lens 6 ✅ → ✅), keeps learnability in line with A3 since       
  there's no pan/zoom UX (lens 4 ⚠️  → ✅), keeps mobile fallback alive because clusters can stack on small screens (lens 7 ❌ → ✅), preserves the anchor fit (lens 5 ✅).
                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  Trade I'm consciously making with A2-prime:                                                                                                                                                             
  - Brief fidelity loss (lens 8 ❌): we ship "tinted clusters on a canvas" instead of "swim lanes." Defensible because the brief's swim-lane language is shorthand for "grouped by kind" — the grouping is
   locked, the visual treatment was always at §4 to decide (and you explicitly said "open to alternatives at §4" in Q3). I'd add a one-line justification to the spec: "§4 chose canvas-with-clusters over
   swim lanes because it forwards-rhymes with F03 + F13."                                                                                                                                                 
  - First-row-of-cards alignment isn't horizontal-by-lane: clusters go in a 2x2 grid (raw top-left, reference top-right, view bottom-left, mv bottom-right). Sam's "scan four lanes left-to-right" muscle 
  memory would now scan four quadrants. Different visual rhythm but same job.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  ---
  My pick: A2-prime                                                                                                                                                                                       
                                      
  Locking it gives you:
  - F01 ships fast (build cost like A3)                                                                                                                                                                   
  - F03 gets a real "drop CSV on canvas" surface                                                                                                                                                          
  - F13 gets a 1:1 inheritance — same shape, same minimap, same vocabulary, just adds React Flow + edges                                                                                                  
  - F01 looks 2027 on Sam's preview-deploy click                                                                                                                                                          
  - Mobile gets free fallback (stack clusters vertically on small screens)                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  If you reject A2-prime and pick a pure direction, my second choice is A3 — for cognitive load + build cost + mobile, accepting the F13 disconnect as a real cost. Pure A1 I'd argue against: it pays the
   brief-fidelity card but loses on every load-bearing lens.

⏺ Active step: §5 Proposed approach — AGENT-LED, requires_user_approval: true, triggers: [section_approved] (this approval gets HASHED into verification.json + appended to decisions.md; future edits    
  require re-approval). The big one.                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  ---                                                                                                                                                                                                     
  §5 Proposed approach — F01 Auth + canvas shell (DRAFT for approval)                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  Built on top of §1-§4 + every Appendix-A invariant (A.1 postgres.js, A.2 jsonParam, A.4 mandatory encryption, A.6 join safety, A.7 UNIQUE indexes, A.16 default tenant constant, A.20 plain-English
  copy).                                                                                                                                                                                                  
                                      
  Recommended approach                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                      
  Build F01 as a Next.js 16 App Router app with two database clients side-by-side: @supabase/ssr for Supabase Auth (cookie-correct, SSR-safe sessions) and postgres.js v3 for every data query (per A.1 — 
  NO ORM). Render /map as a Server Component pulling table metadata via information_schema JOIN pipelogic.table_metadata. Side panel + theme toggle + ⌘K palette are Client Components built on shadcn/ui
  primitives. Migration 0001 creates the three PipeLogic-owned schemas + seeds pipelogic.table_metadata with the kind classification for Topishop's public.* tables.                                      
                                      
  Moving parts:
  - Auth gate — src/proxy.ts (Next.js 16 middleware; per stack.md). Reads Supabase session cookie via @supabase/ssr, checks email against ALLOWED_USER_EMAILS env var, redirects to /login or /not-invited
   on failure.                                                                                                                                                                                            
  - Database access — src/lib/db/pg.ts exports the postgres.js v3 client + the jsonParam(x) helper (per A.2). Every query goes through this module.
  - Default tenant — src/lib/db/metadata.ts exports DEFAULT_TENANT_ID = '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001' (per A.16). Every JOIN / UPSERT against tenant-scoped tables imports this — no inline UUID 
  literals.                                                                                                                                                                                               
  - Schema bootstrap (supabase/migrations/0001_pipelogic_init.sql) — raw .sql, applied manually via Supabase Studio (per stack.md). Creates pipelogic + pl_draft + pl_live. Creates                       
  pipelogic.table_metadata with (tenant_id, schema_name, table_name, kind) + PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, schema_name, table_name) (per A.7 UNIQUE-leads-with-tenant_id). Seeds rows for Topishop's public.*   
  tables.                                                                                                                                                                                                 
  - /map page — Server Component. One SQL query joins information_schema.tables against pipelogic.table_metadata with tenant_id in the ON clause (per A.6). Renders the 4-cluster grid from wireframe.html
   (A2-prime).                                                                                                                                                                                            
  - Side panel — Client Component (shadcn Sheet). On card click, fetches from /api/tables/[schema]/[name]/sample route handler. Route runs SELECT … FROM "<schema>"."<name>" LIMIT 50 with table-name     
  escaping via postgres.js identifier helper (NOT string interpolation — SQL-injection guard).                                                                                                       
  - Theme — next-themes (system-preference auto-switch, B2 from §4).                                                                                                                                      
  - Font — Geist Sans + Geist Mono via Google Fonts CDN (C3 from §4).
  - Test harness — Vitest config + Playwright config + .github/workflows/playwright.yml + .github/workflows/sdd-ci.yml. (Closes the F01-BUILD scaffold gap flagged in stack.md.)

  - Cost — all dependencies free at MVP scale (Supabase / Railway / Sentry / GitHub Actions free tiers). No new vendors beyond /sdd-setup-locked stack.                                                   
  - Complexity — two DB clients side-by-side (@supabase/ssr for auth cookies, postgres.js for data). Module separation: src/lib/auth/ vs src/lib/db/. Modest cost; standard pattern for Supabase + raw-SQL
   projects.                                                                                                                                                                                              
  - Time-to-ship — F01 carries the foundation: scaffold + Tailwind + shadcn + auth + middleware + migration + /map + side panel + filter + theme + test harness + CI. Sized M per brief but may flex to L
  on first build (F02 onward will ride this foundation).                                                                                                                                                  
  - Debt — zero introduced. Every choice aligns with locked stack.md + principles.md + Appendix A invariants.
