⏺ §5 Proposed approach — F01 (plain English, concise) (DRAFT for approval)                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  What we're building                                                                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  A Next.js 16 app with two parts:                                                                                                                                                                        
  1. A login screen. You type your email; if it's on the allowlist you get a magic link. Click it, you're in.                                                                                             
  2. A /map page. Shows every Topishop table as a card, grouped into 4 colored boxes (raw / reference / view / mv). Click any card → side panel slides in with that table's column list and 50 sample     
  rows. Read-only — editing comes in F02.                                                                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  Plus: light/dark mode that follows your OS, ⌘K palette to jump anywhere, Geist font, Supabase login with email allowlist as the front door.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  How the pieces fit (concrete walkthrough)
                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  Imagine Sam at his laptop:                                                                                                                                                                              
  1. He visits pipelogic.app. The middleware (the "bouncer at the door") checks: is there a session cookie? is the email in ALLOWED_USER_EMAILS? No → redirect to /login.
  2. He types sam@topishop.com, clicks "send magic link." Supabase emails it. He clicks. Now he's in.                                                                                                     
  3. He lands on /map. The page asks the database: "give me every table in public.*, plus what kind each one is (raw / reference / view / mv)."
  4. The database returns 28 rows. The page draws them as cards in the 4 colored clusters per the wireframe.                                                                                              
  5. Sam clicks baselinker_orders. The side panel slides in. It runs SELECT … FROM baselinker_orders LIMIT 50. Shows column list + first 50 rows.                                                         
  6. Sam clicks the moon icon → dark mode. Or ⌘K → palette pops up to search tables by name.                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  What we set up first (foundation parts)                                                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  
  │                    Part                     │                                                            What it does, in plain English                                                            │
  ├─────────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤  
  │ src/proxy.ts                                │ The "bouncer." Every request goes through it. Off the allowlist → bounced.                                                                           │
  ├─────────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ src/lib/db/pg.ts                            │ The single place where the app talks to Postgres. All queries go through here so we don't accidentally write the buggy patterns V1 paid for.         │  
  ├─────────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤  
  │ src/lib/db/metadata.ts                      │ One line: DEFAULT_TENANT_ID = '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001'. Every query that filters by tenant imports it from here. When multi-tenant     │  
  │                                             │ ships post-MVP, only this one file changes.                                                                                                          │  
  ├─────────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ supabase/migrations/0001_pipelogic_init.sql │ A .sql file Sam pastes into Supabase Studio. Sets up the 3 PipeLogic-owned drawers (pipelogic / pl_draft / pl_live) + the small index that says      │  
  │                                             │ which Topishop table is which kind.                                                                                                                  │  
  ├─────────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ /map page                                   │ Asks the DB once for the table list, draws the 4 clusters.                                                                                           │  
  ├─────────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤  
  │ Side panel                                  │ Click a card → fetches columns + 50 rows for that table. Read-only.                                                                                  │
  ├─────────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤  
  │ Test harness                                │ Vitest for unit tests, Playwright for click-through tests, runs before every push.                                                                   │
  └─────────────────────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  
                                      
  Alternatives we considered                                                                                                                                                                              
                                      
  1. "Use Supabase's all-in-one tool for the database too."                                                                                                                                               
  Tempting because it's one tool instead of two. We rejected it: V1 had silent data-corruption bugs that ONLY happened with the all-in-one tool's shortcut for tricky data types (jsonb). Those bugs took
  weeks to find. The locked rule (Appendix A.1) is to use a more explicit, verbose pattern that doesn't hide the trap.                                                                                    
                                      
  2. "Use a fancy ORM like Drizzle or Prisma."                                                                                                                                                            
  Same problem — these tools hide the same traps. V1 already wrote a decision document explicitly forbidding them.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  3. "Skip the table-kinds index; figure out raw vs reference later."
  Doesn't work: the database itself can't tell raw apart from reference (it sees both as the same kind of object). We'd have to write code to guess. Cleaner to set up the small index upfront so F02     
  inherits it.                                                                                                                                                                                            
  
  4. "Skip Playwright tests for F01; add them later."                                                                                                                                                     
  Too risky — F01 is the foundation. If it silently breaks at deploy time and we have no click-through smoke test, Sam discovers it via a broken page. Cost: one extra build task. Do it now.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  What we're trading off
                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  - Money: nothing. Everything is free at MVP scale.                                                                                                                                                      
  - Complexity: two database connections side-by-side instead of one. Each has a clear job (login vs data). Modest cost.
  - Time-to-ship: F01 is the longest feature in v1 because it's the foundation. F02-F15 ride this and ship much faster.                                                                                   
  - Technical debt: none introduced. Every choice matches what we locked at /sdd-setup.                                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  What you're paying for / signing off on (each tool in one line)

      271                                                                                                                                                                                                 
      272  - [ ] approval: draft the data contract, iterate with the user, sync data-model.md, get approval                                                                                               
      273                                                                                                                                                                                                 
      274 +#### §6 Data contract                                                                                                                                                                          
      275 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      276 +##### What pieces of information do we need to store                                                                                                                                           
      277 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      278 +F01 is mostly a **read** feature — the app looks at the database and draws cards. It only needs to **store** one thing of its own: a small index that maps each Topishop table to its ki
          +nd (raw / reference / view / mv) so the canvas knows which lane to put it in.                                                                                                           
      279 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      280 +In plain English, for every Topishop table we want to remember:                                                                                                                         
      281 +- **which schema it lives in** (always `public` for now);                                                                                                                               
      282 +- **its name** (e.g. `baselinker_orders`);                                                                                                                                              
      283 +- **its kind** (`raw`, `reference`, `view`, or `mv`) — the only piece the database itself can't figure out;                                                                             
      284 +- **a friendly display name** (optional — falls back to the table name);                                                                                                                
      285 +- **where it sits inside its lane** (a small number so we can re-order cards inside a cluster later);                                                                                   
      286 +- **when the row was created and last updated.**                                                                                                                                        
      287 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      288 +Plus the multi-tenant scaffold (rule A.7): every row carries a `tenant_id` defaulted to the single-tenant constant. Today every row has the same value; when multi-tenant lands post-MVP
          + nothing breaks.                                                                                                                                                                        
      289 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      290 +##### What F01 reads (no writes, no migrations to existing schemas)                                                                                                                     
      291 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      292 +| Source | What the app asks for | Where it lives |                                                                                                                                     
      293 +|---|---|---|                                                                                                                                                                           
      294 +| `information_schema.tables` | the list of `public.*` tables | Postgres (built-in) |                                                                                                   
      295 +| `information_schema.columns` | the column list for one table (side panel) | Postgres (built-in) |                                                                                     
      296 +| `public.<table>` | the first 50 rows of one table (side panel) | Topishop-owned, read-only |                                                                                          
      297 +| `pipelogic.table_metadata` | the kind of each Topishop table | new — defined below |                                                                                                  
      298 +| `auth.users` | the signed-in user's email | Supabase-managed (no DDL from us) |                                                                                                       
      299 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      300 +Topishop's `public.*` schema is read-only from PipeLogic's side. F01 introduces zero new fields on existing entities.                                                                   
      301 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      302 +##### Technical version — the one new entity                                                                                                                                            
      303 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      304 +A new entity `[[entity:TableMetadata]]` lands in `.sdd/data-model.md` under `## Schema: pipelogic`. Full DDL (raw SQL, per A.1) ships in BUILD as `supabase/migrations/0001_pipelogic_in
          +it.sql`:                                                                                                                                                                                
      305 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      306 +```sql                                                                                                                                                                                  
      307 +CREATE TABLE pipelogic.table_metadata (                                                                                                                                                 
      308 +  tenant_id     uuid        NOT NULL DEFAULT '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001',                                                                                                    
      309 +  schema_name   text        NOT NULL,                                                                                                                                                   
      310 +  table_name    text        NOT NULL,                                                                                                                                                   
      311 +  kind          text        NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('raw','reference','view','mv')),                                                                                                   
      312 +  display_name  text,                                                                                                                                                                   
      313 +  cluster_order int         NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,                                                                                                                                         
      314 +  created_at    timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),                                                                                                                                     
      315 +  updated_at    timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),                                                                                                                                     
      316 +  PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, schema_name, table_name)                                                                                                                                      
      317 +);                                                                                                                                                                                      
      318 +```                                                                                                                                                                                     
      319 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      320 +The PRIMARY KEY leads with `tenant_id` (rule A.7 — every UNIQUE/PK index leads with `tenant_id` so multi-tenant doesn't require a re-index later). The `DEFAULT` references the literal 
          +default-tenant constant; in code, `src/lib/db/metadata.ts` exports the same value so SELECTs and INSERTs share one source of truth.                                                     
      321 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      322 +`updated_at` is set by a trigger added in the same migration (boilerplate `BEFORE UPDATE` trigger calling `now()`) — keeps writes ergonomic when F02+ starts updating `kind` or `display
          +_name`.                                                                                                                                                                                 
      323 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      324 +##### How `/map` uses it                                                                                                                                                                
      325 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      326 +One query at page-load:                                                                                                                                                                 
      327 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      328 +```sql                                                                                                                                                                                  
      329 +SELECT t.table_name,                                                                                                                                                                    
      330 +       COALESCE(m.kind, 'raw')          AS kind,                                                                                                                                        
      331 +       COALESCE(m.display_name, t.table_name) AS display_name,                                                                                                                          
      332 +       COALESCE(m.cluster_order, 0)     AS cluster_order                                                                                                                                
      333 +FROM information_schema.tables t                                                                                                                                                        
      334 +LEFT JOIN pipelogic.table_metadata m                                                                                                                                                    
      335 +  ON m.tenant_id    = $defaultTenantId   -- A.6: tenant_id in ON clause, not WHERE                                                                                                      
      336 + AND m.schema_name  = t.table_schema                                                                                                                                                    
      337 + AND m.table_name   = t.table_name                                                                                                                                                      
      338 +WHERE t.table_schema = 'public'                                                                                                                                                         
      339 +  AND t.table_type IN ('BASE TABLE', 'VIEW')                                                                                                                                            
      340 +ORDER BY kind, cluster_order, t.table_name;                                                                                                                                             
      341 +```                                                                                                                                                                                     
      342 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      343 +Rule A.6 enforced at the query level — `tenant_id` in the `ON` clause, not the `WHERE`. The `LEFT JOIN` means a Topishop table that isn't yet in `table_metadata` shows up anyway in the
          + `raw` lane (acceptable fallback per the M1 freshness contract).                                                                                                                        
      344 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      345 +##### Seeding (one row per Topishop table, lands in BUILD)                                                                                                                              
      346 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      347 +The same migration `0001_pipelogic_init.sql` `INSERT`s one `table_metadata` row per current Topishop `public.*` table — pulled from a manual list owned by Sam at first commit. Later fe
          +atures (F09 type-drift) may automate keeping this list fresh; F01 ships the static seed.                                                                                                
      348 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      349 +##### Edge cases at the data layer                                                                                                                                                      
      350 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      351 +| Case | What happens |                                                                                                                                                                 
      352 +|---|---|                                                                                                                                                                               
      353 +| **Table exists in `public.*` but missing from `table_metadata`.** | Renders in the `raw` lane via `COALESCE`. No error. Sam adds a row to fix the lane assignment. |                  
      354 +| **Row exists in `table_metadata` but the `public.*` table is gone.** | Hidden — `INNER` semantics on the FROM side filter it out. Stale row lingers harmlessly until F09 cleans up. | 
      355 +| **Two writers race on `kind`.** | Out of scope for F01 (read-only). When F02+ enables editing, the PK guarantees one row per (tenant, schema, table); last-writer-wins is acceptable f
          +or this metadata. |                                                                                                                                                                     
      356 +| **Multi-tenant cross-tenant leak.** | Prevented by the PK leading with `tenant_id` + the `ON`-clause discipline. Only relevant post-MVP. |                                            
      357 +| **CHECK violation on `kind`.** | INSERT fails with a Postgres CHECK error. Surfaces during the seed migration if a typo slips through — fixed before merge, no runtime path. |        
      358 +| **Side panel queries a table that was just dropped.** | `SELECT … LIMIT 50` returns a Postgres `relation does not exist` error → the side panel shows a friendly "this table is no lon
          +ger in the database" message. F01 catches this once (try/catch around the panel query). |                                                                                               
      359 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      360 +##### What's NOT in §6 for F01                                                                                                                                                          
      361 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      362 +- **No new fields on `auth.users`.** Allowlist gate is env-var-based (`ALLOWED_USER_EMAILS`), not a DB row. Per Q1 grill: F01 ships zero migrations on auth.                            
      363 +- **No `editable_columns` on `table_metadata`.** Editing is F02 — it adds a `text[] editable_columns` column when it lands.                                                             
      364 +- **No `recipe_*` / `joins` / `inbox_items` / `edit_history` / `rules` / `import_run` / `recipe_usage_stats`.** All deferred to their own features per the carry-forward inventory.     
      365 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      366 +##### Wiki-link emission                                                                                                                                                                
      367 +

  What happened while you were away                                                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  1. Fixed the every-turn stop-hook warning. The MCP server wasn't on disk where invariant 8 expected it. I symlinked the plugin install into extensions/sdd-mcp-server/ at the project root and added    
  /extensions/ to .gitignore. The hook will now pass silently and [[slug]] references get checked.                                                                                                        

  The §6 proposal (one-paragraph version)

  F01 is a read feature. The only thing it stores of its own is one tiny index: pipelogic.table_metadata — a row per Topishop public.* table, telling us whether that table is raw / reference / view / mv
   so the canvas knows which of the 4 colored lanes to draw it in. PK leads with tenant_id (rule A.7). Multi-tenant scaffolding from day one with the centralised default constant. F01 introduces zero
  new fields on existing entities and zero migrations on auth.* (the allowlist gate stays env-var-based).

  Six edge cases handled at the data layer (table missing from index → falls into raw lane via COALESCE; index row pointing at deleted table → hidden; dropped-table-during-side-panel-query → friendly
  error; etc).

  What's open / what to look at

  - The full §6 prose is in .sdd/features/001-auth-canvas-shell/spec.md (lines ~272–360).
  - The new entity is in .sdd/data-model.md (#### TableMetadata).
  - Two pre-existing theatre-token lint warnings on data-model.md (lines 5, 16, 56, 127) are in template prose I didn't author — they made it through bootstrap, so they shouldn't block this commit.

  Reply approve to lock §6 + commit, or tell me what to change (e.g. "add source_id for the F05 connector future", "drop display_name — too early", "split kind enum out into a separate lookup table", or
   anything else).

      542 +#### §10 Non-functional                                                                                                                                                                        
      543 +                                                                                                                                                                                               
      544 +Most of these are already locked elsewhere — the job here is to surface the ones that bind F01 directly.                                                                                       
      545 +                                                                                                                                                                                               
      546 +##### Performance                                                                                                                                                                              
      547 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      548 +- **`/map` page-load: ONE round-trip to the database.** The §6 query (a single `LEFT JOIN information_schema.tables ↔ pipelogic.table_metadata`) is the only data fetch the page makes o
          +n initial render. No N+1, no waterfall. {verify-by: a Playwright test that asserts `request.url.includes('/postgres')` count = 1 on `/map` first paint.}                                
      549 +- **Side panel: ONE round-trip per card click.** Columns (`information_schema.columns`) + 50 sample rows fetched in a single batch. Subsequent clicks on the same card may serve from in
          +-memory state during the same `/map` session — no requirement to re-fetch.                                                                                                              
      550 +- **No fixed time budget at MVP.** F01's audience is Sam + 1 ops staffer; a hard p95 doesn't make sense at this volume. Subjective check at SHIP: *"does `/map` feel snappy to Sam at hi
          +s MacBook Air on home WiFi?"* {best-effort: Sam at SHIP — preview-deploy clickthrough.}                                                                                                 
      551 +- **Freshness contract (M3): rows match reality at click-time.** No cache layer in F01; if it ever feels slow at scale, F02+ may add a TTL'd query layer — out of F01's scope.          
      552 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      553 +##### Security                                                                                                                                                                          
      554 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      555 +- **Allowlist gate must NOT leak the list.** Middleware (`src/proxy.ts`) returns the same `/login` page with the same generic message for both *"email not allowlisted"* and *"email all
          +owlisted but typo'd."* The 403 path does not send a magic link, but it also does not surface "this email isn't on the list." Per Flow 1 failure path.                                   
      556 +- **Service-role Supabase key stays server-side.** Client bundle gets only the anon-scoped client. Server actions / route handlers use the service-role key, never inlined into client c
          +omponents. Build-time check: any `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` env var carrying a service-role key is a build failure.                                                                                
      557 +- **AES-256-GCM at-rest for any credentials we store** (per A.4 — locked from V1). F01 stores zero credentials of its own — auth tokens live in Supabase, magic-link state lives in Supa
          +base. The rule binds when F02+ starts persisting connector secrets; F01 inherits the discipline without exercising it.                                                                  
      558 +- **Tenant-id discipline at the code layer** (per A.6 + A.7). Every query that touches a `pipelogic.*` table puts `tenant_id` in the `ON` clause (not `WHERE`); every UNIQUE/PK index le
          +ads with `tenant_id`. F01 ships ONE such query (§6); the test harness asserts the `ON` clause shape. {verify-by: a Vitest unit test that parses the query string and asserts `ON` has th
          +e tenant_id clause.}                                                                                                                                                                    
      559 +- **Rate-limiting on magic links: inherited from Supabase Auth** (100 emails/hour per project, default). F01 adds no extra layer at MVP — at 1-2 humans, the floor is plenty.           
      560 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      561 +##### Compliance                                                                                                                                                                        
      562 +                                                                                                                                                                                        
      563 +- **EU data residency** (per `stack.md` locked from V1). Supabase project in EU, Sentry project in EU, no third-party services that route data outside the EU. Sam is the data controlle
          +r; tenants will be data processors when multi-tenant lands.                                                                                                                             
      564 +- **GDPR Art. 32 (security of processing)** inherits from the AES-256-GCM rule + Supabase's posture. F01 introduces no new GDPR surface — the only PII is the user's own email, typed by
          + the user, stored by Supabase Auth.                                                                                                                                                     
      565 +- **No PII in client-side error tracking.** Sentry's `beforeSend` hook strips email addresses + auth-token fragments from breadcrumbs and stack-trace contexts before sending. {verify-b
          +y: a Vitest unit test that feeds a fake event with an email + JWT into the hook and asserts both are scrubbed.}                                                                         
      566 +- **No third-party analytics / tracking pixels of any kind.** Locked at `/sdd-setup` (no PostHog, no Datadog, no Plausible). F01 ships zero `<script>` tags pointing at non-PipeLogic do
          +mains.                                                                                                                                                                                  
      567 +

  even the project's creator can only see once). The MCP create_project response had no password field, and there's no MCP query to fetch it.                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                 
  So your only path to see/use it is the dashboard's "Reset database password" flow:                                                                                             
                                                                                                                                                                                 
  1. On the Database tab that's already open (/settings/database), look near the top — there's a section called "Database password" with a button "Reset database password" (or  
  "Generate new password").           
  2. Click it → Supabase generates a new password and shows it once on screen.                                                                                                   
  3. Copy it immediately (it's only displayed once; if you close the toast, you reset it again).                                                                                 
  4. Now scroll to Connection string → URI and copy the full URL — it'll have the new password baked in already (or replace [YOUR-PASSWORD] with what you just copied).          
  5. Paste over __PASTE_FULL_DATABASE_URL_FROM_DASHBOARD__ in .env.local.                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                 
  This is a one-time annoyance — once it's in .env.local and Railway env vars (later, at SHIP), nobody touches it again unless you rotate.

⏺ Yes and no — depends what you mean by "in parallel."                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                 
  Short answer                                                                                                                                                                   
   
  You can run F02 SPEC in a parallel session. You CAN'T run F02 BUILD until F01 BUILD finishes — F02 (and every other feature) declares deps: F01 in the project spec. F01's app 
  shell, auth, and /map foundation are what F02-F15 ride on.
                                                                                                                                                                                 
  So the realistic parallel split is:                                                                                                                                            
  - Terminal 1: ralph keeps cooking F01 BUILD (you're already here)
  - Terminal 2 / new Claude session: F02 SPEC ceremonies (spec writing, no code yet)

  Why I wouldn't actually do this right now

  Three reasons:
  1. Shared files conflict. INDEX.md, decisions.md, data-model.md, patterns.md are touched by every feature. Two sessions writing them at once = merge conflicts. SDD's recovery
  is manual and tedious.
  2. F01 has 11 tasks left, ~2-3 hours. That's not worth context-switching for. F02 SPEC also takes 30-60 min to walk; you'd finish around the same time.
  3. Cognitive overhead. F02 builds on what F01 ships (the actual /map shell, the side panel component, the pipelogic.table_metadata table). SPECing F02 cleanly is easier WHEN
  F01 is real and you can click around it.

  If you really want to parallelize

  The technically clean way uses a git worktree so ralph doesn't fight the parallel branch:

  # Create an isolated working dir for F02 — sdd/002-... branch
  git worktree add ../pipelogic_v2-f02 -b sdd/002-side-panel-cell-editing main

  # In a fresh Claude Code session, cd into that worktree
  cd ../pipelogic_v2-f02

  # Start the F02 SPEC walk
  # (Claude reads `Active:` from the branch name, finds features/002-... folder)
  /next

  Two checkouts, one repo, ralph keeps running in the original.

  My recommendation

  Wait for ralph. Spend the time elsewhere — Sentry dashboard tour, Railway dashboard tour, drafting a brief for what F02's editing UX should feel like before you /next into it.
   When F01 lands you'll start F02 fresh with the actual /map open in another tab to design against.

  If you want to start F02 SPEC anyway, say so and I'll walk you through the worktree setup precisely.

  Hard scope decisions (will block §2-§5)                                                                                                                                        
                                      
  1. Which columns are editable, who decides, how locked?                                                                                                                        
  pipelogic.table_metadata.editable_columns is a text[] per the brief. Who fills it — Sam manually for each table? An admin UI later? Defaults inferred from column type (text
  editable, foreign keys not)?                                                                                                                                                   
  2. Edit triggers — what counts as "saving"?
    - Enter to save / Esc to cancel?                                                                                                                                             
    - Save on Tab to next cell (spreadsheet feel)?                                                                                                                               
    - Save on blur (click-away)?                                                                                                                                                 
    - Explicit "Save" + "Cancel" buttons per row?                                                                                                                                
  Pick a primary, accept that others may not work.                                                                                                                               
  3. Conflict policy. Two people open the same cell at the same time. Whose change wins? Last-write-wins (cheapest)? Optimistic lock on updated_at (refuses stale write)?        
  Something fancier? Auth says single-user F01, so this is a "when multi-tenant lights up" decision.                                                                             
  4. Optimistic UI vs pessimistic.                                                                                                                                               
    - Optimistic: cell updates immediately, rollback on server error → snappy but flicker on failure.                                                                            
    - Pessimistic: spinner, wait for server confirm, then commit → slower but always-truthful.                                                                                   
  5. Undo scope. Brief says undo within session, not across refresh. So: in-memory stack only? cmd+Z? Per-cell or per-session? How many undo levels?                             
                                                                                                                                                                                 
  Quieter decisions (will block §6-§7)                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                 
  6. Audit table shape. Beyond previous_value / current_value, what else: user email, IP address, user-agent, source ('inline-edit' vs 'api-batch')? Keep it minimal or capture  
  forensics?
  7. Audit retention. Forever? Rolling 12-month window? Important for storage cost when usage scales.                                                                            
  forensics?
  7. Audit retention. Forever? Rolling 12-month window? Important for storage cost when usage scales.
  8. Type safety. Sam edits quantity (int) — does the UI prevent typing letters, or accept anything and validate server-side? created_at — show a date picker, or raw text?

  UX direction (will block §4 wireframe)

  9. Visual reference. F01 anchored on n8n + Figma + Coda. For inline edits specifically, Linear's table cells, Notion's database cells, Airtable's grid, or Numbers/Excel? Each

           +ation. A determined attacker with a real Supabase JWT for `foo@gmail.com` (not allowlisted) could base64-rewrite the `email` claim to `sam@topishop.com` and t
           +he middleware would let them through. Real reads via `getMapTables` then succeed because the DB connection uses `DATABASE_URL` with project-level credentials.

           +scrubbed. Session IDs in `sb-<ref>-auth-token` cookies aren't recognised. §10 Compliance promises "no PII in client-side error tracking"; the actual scrub is        
           +JWT+email-only.                                                                                                                                                    
       995 +   - **Suggested fix:** add patterns for IPv4 (`\d{1,3}(\.\d{1,3}){3}`), IPv6 (`[a-f0-9:]+`), and Supabase refresh token shape. Or — cheaper — use Sentry's bu
           +ilt-in `denyUrls` + `request.cookies.deny: ['sb-*']` config to block cookies wholesale.

       997 +   - **Where:** `src/lib/db/pg.ts:14`.                                                                                                                        
       998 +   - **What goes wrong:** the 2026-05-07 decisions log entry explicitly chose **session pooler** (port 5432) OVER **transaction pooler** (port 6543) precisely
           + because session mode preserves prepared statements that `postgres.js`'s tagged-template ergonomics rely on. Then the code disabled prepared statements anyway
           +. Either the rationale was wrong, or the code is leaving real perf on the table.                                                                              
       999 +   - **Suggested fix:** if there was a real test failure with `prepare: true`, document it in the file header AND update the 2026-05-07 decisions entry. Other

         + supported) or queries fail mysteriously. — Where: F01 (`[[001-auth-canvas-shell]]`) [PR pending].

      1021  ### action: learn                              
      1022                                                                                                                                                                       
      1023  - [x] summary: F01 ships login + /map canvas + read-only side panel — see §learn.summary below.
      1024 -- [ ] lessons: distill cross-feature lessons + sync patterns.md (next commit).                                                                                       
      1024 +- [x] lessons: 5 lessons synced to `.sdd/patterns.md` — 2 architecture decisions (proxy must verify JWT, pooler/prepare pairing) + 3 pitfalls (T0 bootstrap di
           +scipline, macOS IPv6 trap, adversarial-review-before-BUILD scheduling). Long-form recap below.                                                                       
      1025                            
      1026 +##### §learn.lessons (long-form)                                                                                                                              
      1027 +                                                                                                                                                              
      1028 +**Architecture decision: any middleware/proxy that reads an identity claim from a JWT must verify the signature.** F01's first `src/proxy.ts` decoded the emai
           +l claim locally without verifying — combined with a data path that uses `postgres.js` direct (so Supabase Auth is never re-consulted at the data layer), this 
           +gave any visitor with a valid Supabase JWT a path to rewrite the email and walk past the allowlist. Lesson: don't assume a downstream check will catch unsigne
           +d claims. Sometimes the data layer doesn't.                                                                                                                   
      1029 +                                                                                                                                                              
      1030 +**Architecture decision: Supabase pooler choice is paired with `postgres.js`'s `prepare:` flag.** Session pooler (port 5432, our choice for V2) preserves prep
           +ared statements; transaction pooler (port 6543) doesn't. Wrong pairing = either slow-by-default (prepared disabled when supported) or queries failing in confu
           +sing ways. Track these together when configuring the connection string.                                                                                       
      1031 +                                                                                                                                                              
      1032 +**Pitfall: foundation features need a T0 bootstrap task in §14.** F01's planned build sequence started at T15 (theme toggle) on the assumption "the app shell 
           +exists." It didn't (fresh repo, no `package.json` yet). Ralph halted on iteration 1. Lesson: every first-of-its-kind feature gets an explicit "scaffold runtim
           +e + dependencies" T0 task before any behaviour task lands.                                                                                                    
      1033 +                                                                                                                                                              
      1034 +**Pitfall: macOS direct DB connection to Supabase Postgres is IPv6-only since 2024.** `db.<ref>.supabase.co:5432` silently fails from typical Mac home network
           +s. Use the session pooler at `aws-0-<region>.pooler.supabase.com:5432` with user format `postgres.<ref>` for IPv4-friendly + prepared-statement support.      
      1035 +                                                                                                                                                              
      1036 +**Pitfall: run adversarial-review BEFORE BUILD, not at SHIP.** F01's F1 (the auth bypass) was a design-time miss that BUILD encoded into 26 GREEN tasks; catch
           +ing it at SHIP meant rewriting `proxy.ts` after every test fixture had baked the unsigned-JWT shape into 30+ Playwright tests. For future features: move adver
           +sarial-review to be the last SPEC action (after edge-case-sweep), not the third SHIP action.                                                                  
      1037 +                                                                                                                                                              
      1038  #### §learn.summary
      1039  
      1040  F01 shipped the login surface (Supabase magic-link + email allowlist via `src/proxy.ts`) and the `/map` canvas — every Topishop `public.*` table renders as a
            card, grouped into 4 colored clusters (`raw` / `reference` / `view` / `mv`), with click-to-open side-panel showing columns + 50 sample rows. Built so Sam can
            answer *"do I have a table for X?"* in seconds without `psql` or Supabase Studio. Three real surprises during BUILD: (1) `/map` foundation halted because the
            fresh Supabase project had zero `public.*` tables — synthetic fixture migration filled that gap mid-flow; (2) macOS' IPv4-only network can't reach Supabase's
            IPv6-only direct DB connection — switched to the session pooler with `postgres.<ref>` user format; (3) adversarial-review surfaced a real auth bypass: the pro
            xy decoded JWT email claims without verifying the signature, combined with a data path that bypasses Supabase Auth (postgres.js direct), letting any visitor w
            ith a valid Supabase JWT rewrite the email and walk past the allowlist. All three were caught + fixed before SHIP. What I'd do differently: bake the T0 bootst
            rap task into plan-decompose proactively (so the build sequence doesn't start mid-air), and run adversarial-review BEFORE BUILD instead of at SHIP — the F1 fi
            nding was a design-time miss, not a code bug.

⏺ Update(supabase/migrations/0002_seed_public_fixture.sql)
  ⎿  Added 14 lines, removed 4 lines                                                      
       97    ('GLS-FAKE-003', 'TEST-GLS-12347', 11.20)                                                                                                                           
       98  ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;                                                        
       99                                                                                                                                                                        
      100 -INSERT INTO public.gls_tracking_routes (tracking, route_step, scanned_at) VALUES                                                                               
      101 -  ('TEST-GLS-12345', 'collected', '2026-04-15 10:00:00+00'),                                                                                                          
      100 +-- 2026-05-08 fix (CodeRabbit E): bigserial PK + ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING is a                                                                                          
      101 +-- silent dup-creator — each re-run mints fresh ids, so the PK conflict never                                                                                         
      102 +-- fires. Use WHERE NOT EXISTS against a natural key (tracking + route_step)                                                                                          
      103 +-- so the seed is genuinely idempotent for tables with auto-generated PKs.                                                                                            
      104 +INSERT INTO public.gls_tracking_routes (tracking, route_step, scanned_at)

❯ i am not on the free tier am i?                                                                                                                                                

⏺ Correct — you're on Supabase Pro ($25/mo base + the $10/mo we authorized for pipelogic-v2). I was sloppy saying "free tier."

  But here's the catch: plan tier and email rate-limits are separate things on Supabase.

  Two different limits at play

  1. Plan tier — what you pay for (database size, MAU count, storage, etc.). Pro covers you well above F01's needs.
  2. Auth email rate-limits — separate, project-level, and they exist on all tiers including Pro by default. Defaults are something like 30 OTP emails per hour per project,
  configurable in the dashboard.
  3. Default SMTP — Supabase ships a built-in SMTP relay (mail.app.supabase.io) that BOTH free AND Pro projects use until you configure custom SMTP. That relay has its OWN
  per-project hourly limit (~20-30 emails/hour) that's independent of your plan tier. This is the most likely culprit.

  What to do

  Short term (now):
  - Wait 15-30 min, then retry. The window will reset.
  - Check browser cookies — you may still have a valid session from your earlier successful login. Just hit /map directly.

  Medium term (before real users):
  Set up custom SMTP via Resend / AWS SES / Postmark. Supabase dashboard → Authentication → SMTP Settings. Free Resend tier (3,000 emails/mo) is plenty.

⏺ Cookie dump tells me everything. F01 has a real auth-flow bug.
                                                                                          
  Diagnosis                                                                                                                                                                      
                                                            
  You have:                                                                                                                                                                      
  - ✅ sb-dewvvddmqzsibqpkfzqg-auth-token-code-verifier (half of PKCE flow, set when you requested the magic link — V2 project)                                                  
  - ❌ NO sb-dewvvddmqzsibqpkfzqg-auth-token.0/.1 (the actual session cookie that would log you in)                                                                              
  - (You ARE logged into the V1 topeshop-platform project — those muonacabmh... cookies — but that's irrelevant for V2.)                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                 
  What's missing: the /auth/callback route. Supabase's modern PKCE flow requires:                                                                                                
  1. Form sets code-verifier cookie ← happens (you have this)                                                                                                                    
  2. User clicks email link → Supabase verify endpoint                                                                                                                           
  3. Supabase redirects to http://localhost:3001/?code=<token>                                                                                                                 

  F01 only has /login, /map, /api/signout, /api/table/[name]. Step 4 has nowhere to land. Magic-link arrives, you click it, Supabase verifies, redirects you back, but the app
  has no handler that reads ?code=... and finishes the exchange. CodeRabbit's J finding warned this exact gap ("real-Supabase verified path has zero automated coverage").

  Filing as a hotfix

  This is a [BUG] on F01. Building the fix now on a new branch.
